entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The petitioners are sought to be prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 408,
420, 468 read with Section 34 of IPC.

2. The case of the prosecution is that the petitioner No.1 had created a power of attorney, and based on the power of attorney, conveyed the subject property belonging to the firm, in favour of petitioner Nos.2 and 3.
The petitioners have annexed the memorandum of settlement under Section 89 of CPC read with Rules 24 and 25 of the Karnataka Civil Procedure (Mediation) Rules, 2005.
3. The parties are present before this Court.

4. Perusal of the memorandum of settlement indicated that the parties have amicably resolved the dispute among themselves in Com.Ex.No.487/2022, and as per the terms of the settlement,
petitioner No.1 has agreed pay a sum of Rs.20,00,000/- to respondent No.2 towards full and final settlement, out of which Rs.10,00,000/- is already paid before the Execution Court, and the balance amount of Rs.10,00,000/- will be paid by tomorrow through demand draft or through RTGS.
The respondent No.2 has agreed to withdraw all the allegations and has no objection for quashing the impugned proceedings.
The petitioner has handed over the documents relating to the partnership firm to the de-facto complainant who is present before this court, the receipt of which is duly acknowledged.

Though the offences alleged are cognizable and non compoundable, however, having regard to the fact that the parties have amicably resolved the dispute among themselves, and the respondent No.2 having agreed to withdraw all the allegations, it would be a futile exercise, if the petitioners are subjected to trial, since the probability of the conviction is remote and bleak.
Therefore, the continuation of the criminal proceedings will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i. Criminal Petition is allowed.
ii. The impugned proceedings in CC.No.116/2019 on the file of III Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, at Bengaluru stands quashed.
